name: xlispstat
desc: Statistical data science environment based on Lisp
why: A Lisp-based statistics environment from the 1990s, an old-school environment with real oddity value.

brief.what_it_is: Lisp-Stat is an extensible statistical computing environment for data analysis, teaching, and research, built on a subset of Common Lisp. It extends standard Lisp arithmetic to work element-wise on lists and vectors, and adds basic statistical and linear algebra functions. Its main emphasis is dynamic graphics, delivered through a portable window system meant to behave the same across Mac OS, X Window System, and Microsoft Windows. The homepage does not spell out input or output formats beyond data analysis and graphics.
brief.why_it_exists: The page frames it as a statistical computing environment for data analysis, statistical instruction and research, with an emphasis on providing a framework for exploring dynamic graphical methods. Extensibility is achieved by building on Lisp, and many design choices were motivated by the S language.
brief.how_it_works: A prototype-based object-oriented programming system implements the graphics system and lets users customize and adapt it. The same object system is the basis for statistical model representations, including linear and nonlinear regression and generalized linear models. Element-wise arithmetic on lists and vectors is added on top of standard Common Lisp.
brief.install_notes: The homepage has an 'Obtaining Lisp-Stat' section, but I did not follow it, so I have no details on installation, runtimes, or first-run steps. From the metadata, the installed executable is named xlispstat.
brief.standout: It is an S-inspired statistics system built on Lisp, with dynamic graphics as its core focus and a prototype object system underpinning both the graphics and the regression models. That combination is unusual compared with the scripting-first statistics tools people usually reach for.
brief.status: Unknown from what I read. The homepage is dated 1998-10-07 and shows no release or commit information. The Homebrew formula's existence is metadata only, not evidence of current upkeep. The scout note describes it as a 1990s environment.
brief.caveats: The homepage is dated 1998, so the platform list (Mac OS, X Window System, Microsoft Windows) reflects that era and I could not confirm it runs on current systems. I did not fetch the Obtaining, Documentation, or Bibliography pages, so the install path and docs are unverified. The page names a Lisp-Stat documentation section but gives no URL for it. No licensing information was seen.
quotes: Lisp-Stat is an extensible statistical computing environment for data analysis, statistical instruction and research, with an emphasis on providing a framework for exploring the use of dynamic graphical methods.
Extensibility is achieved by basing Lisp-Stat on the Lisp language, in particular on a subset of Common Lisp.
Many aspects of the system design were motivated by the S language [1].
